title: Hearty Velvety Japanese Pork Tonkotsu Ramen
description: A fatty and velvety Japanese ramen dish featuring raisins and pork, made in a cazuela vessel, this recipe is ayurvedic-rajasic-friendly and perfect for a cold winter night.

ingredients.name: pork bones
ingredients.notes: you can also use pork neck bones or rib bones

instructions: In a large cazuela, heat the oil over medium heat and sear the pork bones until browned on all sides.
Add the sliced onion to the cazuela and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and sliced ginger to the cazuela and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the pork shoulder to the cazuela and cook until it is browned on all sides.
Add the raisins, soy sauce, and sesame oil to the cazuela and stir to combine.
Pour in 4 cups of water and bring the mixture to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer the mixture for 4 hours, or until the pork is tender and the broth is rich and creamy.
Cook the tonkotsu ramen noodles according to the package instructions and slice the cooked pork into thin strips.
To serve, place some noodles in a bowl, add slices of pork, and ladle the hot broth over the top.
Garnish with sliced green onions and serve immediately.
